icpc.global 'The Early Years' list (compiled by Marsha Poucher): 1984 ACM Contest Finals, 15 Feb 1984, Philadelphia - only top 3 named, all North American. Shows no European team in the known part of the field; neither proves nor disproves a 1983 ERC.

leads: Felix 1983-84 is now exhausted (round 3, no mention). Remaining Felix gaps are outside this entry: 677-688, 690-691 (autumn 1984), 696-704, 729-733, 778-790.

NEW: the European regional is now documented for 1984 (Imperial College won; Felix 692, https://issues.felixonline.co.uk/felix_692.pdf) and 1985 (2 Nov 1985; Felix 720/728). Neither Felix item calls the contest the first/second/third, so they neither confirm nor refute a 1983 edition.

Felix (Imperial College Union newspaper) is fully scanned at https://issues.felixonline.co.uk/felix_<N>.pdf (60 MB each, text layer; pdftotext works). Calibration: 689 = 30 Nov 1984, 692 = 18 Jan 1985, 695 = 8 Feb 1985, 699 = 8 Mar 1985, 708 = 19 Jun 1985, 720 = 8 Nov 1985, 726 = 17 Jan 1986, 728 = 24 Jan 1986. Unchecked and worth a pass: 690-691 (Dec 1984), 696-704 (WF 1985 report), 729-733 (WF 1986 report), ~655-665 (autumn 1983), ~748-756 (Nov-Dec 1986), ~780-790 (Nov-Dec 1987, London). For 1983 specifically: issues of Nov 1983-Mar 1984 (roughly 655-675; search engine surfaced 667 and 669 without confirmed content).

Named ACM officials (Felix 692, Jan 1985): Tim McNally 'ACM Chairman, UK' and Bob Parsloe 'ACM Chairman, Europe' presented the 1984 prize - so the early ERCs were run by the ACM UK chapter / ACM European regional representative, not a university. Search ACM UK Chapter newsletters and BCS Computer Bulletin under those names.

1984 Finals (15 Feb 1984, Philadelphia): icpc.global early-years page lists only the top 3 (Johns Hopkins, Virginia Tech, Alberta) and results-1984 is empty, so presence/absence of a European team is still undetermined.

Comer, Rinewalt, Ryan, Poucher: 'The ACM Scholastic Programming Contest - 1977 to 1990', SIGCSE Bulletin 22(1), 1990 (SIGCSE '90 proceedings, p.256; dblp key PoucherCRR90) - the most likely print source to say when the European region started and which European team (if any) went to the Feb 1984 Philadelphia finals. dl.acm.org refused automated fetch; needs a human with ACM DL access.

CACM / SIGCSE Bulletin 1984 reports on the 1984 ACM Contest Finals (15 Feb 1984, Philadelphia; winner Johns Hopkins) - check finalist list for a European team; the icpc.global WF2000 factsheet lists only winners for the 1980s.

Early ERCs may not have been Dutch-hosted: a Dutch newspaper (Algemeen Dagblad 1987-12-10, 'Tweede plaats vakgroep VU', http://resolver.kb.nl/resolve?urn=KBPERS01:003488009:mpeg21:a00070:ocr) reports the 1987 European contest was held in LONDON with 17 teams, VU Amsterdam 2nd (Allis, Foppema, Kaashoek, Langendoen) and qualifying for the finals. So look for 1983-86 in UK sources (British newspaper archives, BCS / ACM UK chapter newsletters, Computer Weekly / Computing 1983) rather than Dutch ones.

Best finding is a probable catalogue correction: the '1990 Mountain Region' problem set now under rmc-1990 most likely belongs to rmc-1989. taiwan-1994.notes: No source for an actual 1994 regional contest in Taiwan was found. Evidence points to there being NO joint Far East/Asia regional in fall 1994: the Jan-1995 usenet regionals list gives the Far East site as 'To Be Announced' with no date while every other region has one; SCMP shows that in the previous season the region's two finals slots were filled by per-chapter contests (Hong Kong chapter contest + Taiwan), and the 1995 finalists are again exactly one Taiwan team (Tsing Hua) and one Hong Kong team (HKU); two Taiwanese sources date the Taiwan-hosted Asia regional from 1995. So taiwan-1994 is probably a Taiwan-only selection (not an 'Asia regional'), whose winner/representative was National Tsing Hua University; host, date and name remain unrecovered. The same reasoning may apply to taiwan-1993 (worth re-checking what that entry represents). Seven teams go to SEERC 2026 (Thessaloniki, 11-13 Dec): those three plus ucunculer, itu.exe, BU Sefer Affetmiyoz, Sienne Staigas. Final stats: 265 submissions, 81 accepted; problems H and K unsolved. Status should change from 'upcoming' to held. The catalogue note 'series resumes after no 2024-25 editions' looks wrong: inzva ran OPC 2024 and TPC 2025 (see leads).
